chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Gloria Lynne walks off stage at Basin Street West and fires him
summary: In California her erratic behavior leads the club owner (Wilt Chamberlain) to intervene, and she fires him and refuses to pay his way home.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But that was quite an experience, and it ended my days with Dakota Staton. It wasn't long after that, that I got a call from Gloria Lynne. I had an engagement with her in California. This turned out to be a rather strange kind of engagement, because I don't know what happened out there, but Gloria's behavior was very erratic. The club started off with people just loving her to death, the business was good, the place was packed and everything. But I never did understand quite what happened out there. After about the second night, she started...she would go on stage and do two or three numbers, then just walk off and not do anything else. So finally, it wound up with the manager having to call Wilt Chamberlain, the basketball, who owned the club -- the club was called Basin Street West. At that particular time, I think he was also the owner of Small's Paradise in New York. He had to call him, and there was quite a bit of controversy.
In the interim of all this, in my attempt to find out what was happening and talk to her, she seemed intimidated by

me... She and I had an argument, and she told me I was fired. So I made mention of the fact that I was in California, and what was I going to do about going back home. So she promptly told me that she didn't care what I did about getting back home!
